notes: ἀνθρώπινον heads on men under rule 66's generic-completion test, after the manner of being the supplied frame; rule 99's contrast (a noun whose own English is manner of X) does not arise.
ὥσπερ … οὕτως: the comparative keeps a bare as and the correlative adverb takes even so whole, headed on so (rule 100). No answering καί stands, so rule 82's bare-even arm is not in question.
The repeated to before the second dative ἀνομίᾳ is a rule 7 helper on the member it introduces, not added (rule 103).
